name: Low Desert Loop — January
subtitle: Death Valley · Route 66 · Palm Springs · Anza-Borrego · Joshua Tree · Lake Havasu
summary: A clockwise loop out of Las Vegas that never climbs out of the warm. Death Valley first, then down across the Mojave onto Route 66, over to the Coachella Valley and Anza-Borrego, up to Joshua Tree, and home along the Colorado River. Nothing on this route sleeps above 2,200 feet, so no night is expected to freeze. Two versions are priced: a motorhome build and a car-plus-hotels build.
startEnd: Las Vegas, NV (Harry Reid International — LAS)

mustSee.name: Zabriskie Point
mustSee.why: Golden badlands at sunset, ten minutes from where you sleep. The best view in Death Valley for the least effort.

mustSee.name: Badwater Basin
mustSee.why: The lowest point in North America, 282 ft below sea level, at 65°F in January. Walk out onto the salt flats.

mustSee.name: Mesquite Flat Dunes
mustSee.why: Go at sunrise. Dunes the kids can run down, before the wind picks up and the light goes flat.

mustSee.name: Elmer's Bottle Tree Ranch
mustSee.why: Free, on the old Route 66 alignment, and unlike anything else on any of these routes. Ten minutes, and worth the detour.

mustSee.name: Palm Springs Aerial Tramway
mustSee.why: Ten minutes from the valley floor to 8,500 feet. The only snow anyone will see on this trip, and you choose whether to go up to it.

mustSee.name: Galleta Meadows
mustSee.why: A 350-foot steel serpent crossing a road in the desert, and 129 other sculptures. Free, and the best surprise on the route.

mustSee.name: The Slot
mustSee.why: A slot canyon you walk yourself, with no permit and no guide. The Southwest Loop pays about $580 for six to do this at Antelope.

mustSee.name: Cholla Cactus Garden
mustSee.why: Ten acres of teddy-bear cholla lit from behind at the end of the day. A quarter-mile loop, and the best photograph in Joshua Tree.

mustSee.name: Skull Rock
mustSee.why: Right beside the road, and the one every child on this trip will want a photograph of.

mustSee.name: Roy's Motel, Route 66
mustSee.why: One neon sign in an abandoned town in the middle of the Mojave. This is the one the kids will talk about.

watchOuts.title: Book Palm Springs first, then Borrego, then Havasu
watchOuts.text: Book Palm Springs first, then Borrego Springs, then Lake Havasu. January is high season in the Coachella Valley — the exact opposite of the Southwest Loop, where the cold made everything cheap. Death Valley and Twentynine Palms have far more slack.

watchOuts.title: It is warm, not hot
watchOuts.text: No night on this route is expected to freeze. The coldest stops are Barstow and Twentynine Palms, both around 2,000 feet, where January lows average the high 30s. A cold snap can put either a degree or two below freezing for a few hours before dawn, so pack for 35°F nights — but there is no sustained freeze anywhere, and nothing here needs winterising.

watchOuts.title: Font's Point is a four-wheel-drive road
watchOuts.text: The road to Font's Point is four miles of soft sand off the Borrego Salton Seaway. It needs four-wheel drive and it strands two-wheel-drive vehicles regularly. A minivan will not make it. Either rent something suitable for the day, take a local jeep tour, or accept that this one is off the list.

watchOuts.title: Death Valley is still closing roads
watchOuts.text: Flood damage persists. Bonnie Clare Road and Scotty's Castle are closed with no reopening date, North Highway has loose gravel and missing shoulders, southern Badwater Road has soft shoulders and unpaved sections, and Emigrant Campground is closed indefinitely. Check the park's conditions page a week before departure.

watchOuts.title: California fuel costs more — fill up before you cross
watchOuts.text: California fuel runs well above Nevada and Arizona. Fill up in Nevada before you drive in, top off in Barstow rather than inside Death Valley, where in-park fuel at Furnace Creek is notably expensive, and fill again in Arizona on the way home.

watchOuts.title: The park pass does not cover the state parks
watchOuts.text: The America the Beautiful pass covers Death Valley and Joshua Tree. It does not cover Anza-Borrego or the Salton Sea, which are California state parks, or Lake Havasu, which is an Arizona state park. None of them are expensive; they are just not free.

watchOuts.title: The Oatman Highway is not for everybody
watchOuts.text: The Oatman Highway over Sitgreaves Pass is steep with blind hairpins, and most rental agreements effectively prohibit it. It is passable but tight in a car and out of the question in a motorhome. The I-40 route to Kingman is the one in the plan.

watchOuts.title: Price the unlimited-miles package
watchOuts.text: If the rental charges per mile at around $0.35, 1,365 miles adds roughly $480. Always price the unlimited-miles package as an alternative.

pros: No night is expected to freeze. Nothing on this route sleeps above 2,200 feet, and the coldest stop averages a low in the high 30s.
Two national parks, three state parks and 200 miles of original Route 66, out and back from a single airport.
Short days: 98 miles a day on average, and six of the fourteen days involve no driving between towns at all.
January is the best month of the year to be in the low desert. Palm Springs runs to the low 70s and Death Valley to the mid-60s.
The motorhome stops being a compromise. Its worst problem on the Southwest Loop was seven freezing nights, and this route does not have one.
One set of flights, one vehicle, one loop. Nothing is one-way.
cons: Two national parks instead of five. The warm places are the low places, and the famous parks are nearly all high.
January is high season in the Coachella Valley, so Palm Springs is the one expensive stop — the reverse of the Southwest Loop, where the cold made everything cheap.
Day 4 and day 11 are both around 177 miles of mostly empty desert. That is the price of a loop this wide.
Font's Point needs four-wheel drive — four miles of soft sand. Neither build reaches it.
Death Valley still has flood damage: Scotty’s Castle and Bonnie Clare Road are closed indefinitely, and several roads have soft shoulders and unpaved sections.
No red rock. This is a route of salt flats, palms, cholla and lava — if what you wanted was Zion and Monument Valley, take the Southwest Loop and dress for it.

notConsidered.place: Zion, Bryce and the Grand Canyon
notConsidered.reason: The famous parks on the Southwest Loop sit between 4,000 and 8,000 feet. Warm and high do not go together in January — that is the entire reason this route exists.
5,200 feet, freezing at night in January, and on the wrong side of the map. It belongs to the Southwest Loop.
Warmer still, and the giant saguaro grows nowhere on this route. But reaching Tucson from Las Vegas costs you a 288-mile day. That trip is the Sonoran Loop.
No hookups, no potable water, no cell service, and the York Fire burned close to 100,000 acres in 2023 including much of the Cima Dome Joshua tree forest.
Genuinely remarkable, and only twenty minutes past the south end of the Salton Sea — but it sits on the far shore and adds about 70 miles to the shortest day of the trip.
A 110-mile round trip from Furnace Creek for a single crater. It fits when Death Valley gets four nights, not three.
Trailer rentals do not include a tow vehicle, and the major rental companies prohibit towing outright. Turo treats towing as a prohibited use that voids damage protection.

moneySavers.detail: Day use is $10 at the visitor centre and campground, and The Slot, Font's Point and every roadside trailhead are free. The Southwest Loop's equivalent — a guided slot canyon at Antelope — runs about $580 for six.
A hundred and thirty life-size metal sculptures — sloths, raptors, horses and a 350-foot serpent — scattered across open land around Borrego Springs. No gate, no ticket, no opening hours.

moneySavers.item: Twentynine Palms instead of inside Joshua Tree
moneySavers.detail: The park's own campgrounds have no hookups, no dump and mostly no water. A full-hookup site in town costs about the same as a dry site inside and you can shower — and you are ten minutes from the north entrance either way.
Buy bedding and kitchen gear at a Las Vegas store on day one for $200-300 and leave it behind. Cheaper than per-person kit fees for six.

moneySavers.item: Go midweek in the Coachella Valley
moneySavers.detail: January is peak season in Palm Springs and the weekend premium is steep. Arriving Sunday or Monday rather than Friday is the single biggest lever in the lodging line.

Covers Death Valley and Joshua Tree — both national parks on this route. It does NOT cover Anza-Borrego or the Salton Sea, which are California state parks, or Lake Havasu, which is an Arizona state park.

options.name: Motorhome
options.tagline: Cheapest, simplest, and no longer the cold one
options.summary: Transport and lodging in one vehicle, so there is nothing to book at six separate stops and you cook instead of eating out. On the Southwest Loop the catch was seven freezing nights; here there are none, and only two stops on the whole route it cannot reach.

vehicle.detail: Cruise America C30 · sleeps 7 · 7 seatbelts · 30 ft long, 8.33 ft wide, 12.2 ft high
vehicle.notes: Book by seatbelt count, not sleeping capacity. On this route there is no reason to take the smaller C25 for clearance — the only length limit you meet is Death Valley's 25 ft on Artist's Drive and Dante's View, and a C25 measures 24.93 ft, which is a three-inch margin you should not rely on.

2.label: Not in the motorhome:
2.text: Artist's Drive is closed to vehicles over 25 ft. Take the separate rental car — it is in the budget for exactly this.

3.label: Not in the motorhome:
3.text: The final climb to Dante's View has the same 25 ft limit. Rental car again. These two are the only places on the whole route the motorhome cannot go.

8.label: Not in the motorhome:
8.text: Font's Point — four miles of soft sand off the Borrego Salton Seaway. Nothing without four-wheel drive gets there, so this one is out for the car build too.

9.label: You sleep in town, not in the park.
9.text: Joshua Tree's own campgrounds cap at around 25 to 35 ft and have no hookups, no dump station and mostly no water. A full-hookup site in Twentynine Palms costs about the same and you are ten minutes from the north entrance. The park roads themselves are fine in a 30-footer.

13.label: Not in the motorhome:
13.text: The Oatman Highway over Sitgreaves Pass — steep, blind hairpins, no room for a 30-footer. The map shows the I-40 route through Kingman, which is the one in the plan and 23 miles shorter anyway.

options.name: Car and lodging
options.tagline: More expensive, more comfortable, and it unlocks the Oatman Highway
options.summary: A seven-seater and a room every night. It costs meaningfully more, and almost all of the gap is food and lodging — but on this route it buys comfort rather than warmth, because the motorhome is not cold here either.

vehicle.detail: Chrysler Pacifica · Honda Odyssey · Chevrolet Suburban · 7 seats
vehicle.notes: A minivan is better for people, a Suburban better for luggage. Fourteen days from Las Vegas including airport concession fees. Neither will get you to Font's Point — that needs four-wheel drive.

costs.notes: "Best value" goes midweek in Palm Springs, sleeps in Barstow rather than a resort, and takes motels over rental houses. "Best location" puts you in the Coachella Valley proper, on the lake at Havasu, and inside Borrego Springs rather than out at the edge.

pros: Unlocks the Oatman Highway and its burros on the way home
Real beds, and rooms you can spread six people across
No dump station, no propane, no levelling blocks
Artist's Drive and Dante's View without a second rental
cons: Roughly $2,000 to $5,300 more than the motorhome
Six separate lodging bookings to manage, in the region's most expensive month
Luggage for six in one vehicle for two weeks is tight

8.label: Still not open to you:
8.text: Font's Point needs four-wheel drive — four miles of soft sand, and it strands two-wheel-drive vehicles regularly. A minivan will not make it. This is the one place on the route neither build reaches without renting something else for the day.

13.text: The Oatman Highway. 23 miles longer, an hour slower, and the wild burros come to the car window. Check the rental agreement first — many of them effectively prohibit Sitgreaves Pass. The map shows the detour.

days.headline: Below sea level by lunchtime
days.notes: Pick up the vehicle and drive straight in. Furnace Creek sits 190 feet below sea level and is the warmest place you will sleep all trip — January highs in the mid-60s, lows around 40.

days.headline: Out of the valley and onto Route 66
days.notes: The one leg that looks dull on the map, and is not. You leave Death Valley by the southern road, cross the Mojave and land on the original alignment of Route 66. Calico is a silver town that went bust in 1896 and was rebuilt as a park — kitsch, and the kids will love it.

pois.name: Calico Ghost Town
pois.caption: A silver town that went bust in 1896, rebuilt as a park.

photos.caption: A silver town that went bust in 1896, rebuilt as a park.

days.headline: Into the warmest air on the trip
days.notes: Start on the old road for Elmer's Bottle Tree Ranch — a forest of welded steel trees hung with thousands of glass bottles, free, and unlike anything else on either route. Then over the pass and down into the Coachella Valley, which runs to the low 70s in January.

pois.caption: A forest of steel trees hung with thousands of glass bottles. Free, on the old road.

photos.caption: A forest of steel trees hung with thousands of glass bottles. Free, on the old road.

days.headline: Palms, and snow you can go and look at
days.notes: The tramway climbs from 2,600 feet to 8,500 in ten minutes. You can be in shirtsleeves at the bottom and in snow at the top on the same afternoon, which is the only snow anybody will see on this trip. Indian Canyons is Agua Caliente land — a real palm oasis in a desert canyon, on a walk that suits everyone.

days.headline: Down the Salton Sea into Anza-Borrego
days.notes: A short day along the west shore of the Salton Sea — a lake 230 feet below sea level that exists only because an irrigation canal broke in 1905 and took two years to close. Borrego Springs is a town of three thousand people surrounded on every side by the largest state park in California.

days.headline: Six hundred thousand acres of state park
days.notes: Borrego Palm Canyon is a three-mile round trip to a palm grove and, in a wet year, a waterfall. The Slot is a genuine slot canyon you walk yourself — no permit, no guide, no fee. Font's Point looks out over the Borrego Badlands and is the best view in the park, but the road to it is four miles of soft sand.

days.headline: Up out of the low desert to Joshua Tree
days.notes: You climb about 1,500 feet, and this is the first night that feels properly cool — high 30s rather than the high 40s you have had. Come in by the south entrance and the Cholla Cactus Garden is the first thing you meet.

days.headline: A full day in Joshua Tree
days.notes: Two deserts meet inside this park — the low Colorado and the high Mojave — and the Joshua trees only grow on the high side. Nearly everything worth doing is a short walk from a car park, which is exactly what you want on day ten with six people.

days.headline: Amboy Crater and the empty Route 66
days.notes: North on Amboy Road onto the loneliest surviving stretch of Route 66. Amboy Crater is a 250-foot cinder cone you can walk into. Roy's Motel is one neon sign in an empty town and it is the photograph everybody takes. Then east to the Colorado River.

days.headline: A day on the water
days.notes: Lake Havasu runs to the mid-60s in January — warm enough to be out on a boat, too cold to swim. London Bridge is the actual bridge that stood over the Thames from 1831: bought from the City of London in 1968, taken apart, and rebuilt here block by numbered block.

days.headline: Route 66 and the dam
days.notes: Up to Kingman, where Route 66 crosses the highway, then down US-93 to Hoover Dam and into Las Vegas. In a car you can take the Oatman Highway instead — 23 miles longer, an hour slower, and the wild burros come to the window.
